name: Customer Journey Mapping (Prescriptive Blueprint)
description: Plane 1 of the CXOS Journey Triad — prescriptive, normative design of what the organization HOPES and plans will happen across a customer journey: persona and Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) intent framing, Golden Path stage blueprints, Moments of Truth (MoT), planned channel swimlanes, target stage SLA and effort budgets, designed fallback and exception branches, and expected emotion curves.
roleInCenter: Normative journey architect: codifies the target Golden Path, stage SLA budgets, and handoff contracts that Plane 2 (journey_tracking) audits for empirical drift and Plane 3 (journey_orchestration) enforces in real time.

glossary.definition: Versioned, machine-readable architectural specification of the intended end-to-end customer journey across personas, stages, channels, and supporting backstage systems
The primary designed sequence of customer stages and channel touchpoints that achieves true resolution with minimum customer effort and optimal unit cost
Outcome-oriented articulation of the underlying functional, emotional, and social job the customer is trying to accomplish, independent of internal department boundaries
High-stakes inflection stage in the journey blueprint where interaction quality disproportionately determines trust, retention, or long-term loyalty
Prescriptive allocation of journey stages across self-service web, mobile app, conversational AI, asynchronous messaging, and assisted voice lanes with explicit context-bridge contracts

glossary.term: Stage Transition SLA & Customer Effort Budget
glossary.definition: Quantitative ceiling assigned to each blueprint stage specifying maximum acceptable latency, customer wait time, authentication steps, and channel switches
Pre-engineered alternate route in the journey blueprint that gracefully handles low NLU confidence, policy exceptions, out-of-hours arrival, or backend outages without stranding the customer
Prescriptive curve plotting anticipated customer anxiety, relief, and confidence across each stage of the blueprint to guide empathy cues and proactive reassurance
Visible interfaces, prompts, notifications, and live agent dialogs directly experienced by the customer above the line of visibility in a service blueprint
Internal API workflows, A2A specialist delegations, CRM state mutations, and WFM queue allocations below the line of visibility required to fulfill frontstage promises
Formal specification of the customer trigger, identity state, and segment eligibility criteria that instantiate a specific journey blueprint
Customer-validated condition proving the underlying Job-to-be-Done is genuinely complete and verified free of downstream repeat contacts within the audit window

facets.name: Journey Blueprint Structural Anatomy
facets.description: Core structural layers composing a machine-executable customer journey blueprint from persona framing down to backstage choreography

children.name: Persona & JTBD Intent Archetypes
children.description: Customer segment profiles paired with functional and emotional Jobs-to-be-Done

children.name: Functional Job Specification
children.description: Concrete task outcome the customer seeks to complete such as disputing a charge or activating hardware

children.name: Emotional & Trust Goal
children.description: Target psychological state such as peace of mind during fraud lockouts or billing shocks

children.name: Persona Vulnerability & Accessibility Profile
children.description: Designed accommodations for elderly, stressed, or assistive-technology customers

children.name: Lifecycle Macro-Phases & Micro-Stage Graphs
children.description: Hierarchical decomposition of customer lifecycle phases into directed acyclic stage transition graphs

children.name: Lifecycle Macro-Phase Node
children.description: High-level journey horizon covering onboarding, routine usage, exception recovery, and renewal

children.name: Micro-Stage Directed Graph
children.description: Granular step-by-step state nodes with explicit entry guards, SLA timers, and transition predicates

children.name: Moment of Truth Gate
children.description: Designated critical stage requiring elevated quality assurance and zero context loss

children.name: Frontstage vs Backstage Service Swimlanes
children.description: Vertical alignment of customer-visible touchpoints with underlying agent, bot, and system dependencies

children.name: Frontstage Customer Touchpoint Lane
children.description: UI screens, voice prompts, and live conversations experienced directly by the customer

children.name: Frontline Agent & Co-Pilot Swimlane
children.description: Desktop guidance, knowledge cards, and wrap-up workflows supporting human handling

children.name: Backstage System & A2A Choreography Lane
children.description: Sub-second API calls, multi-agent A2A task delegations, and asynchronous fulfillment jobs

facets.name: Prescriptive Path Classifications
facets.description: Normative taxonomy of designed routes through a journey blueprint across primary, recovery, proactive, and compliance scenarios

children.name: Primary & Proactive Resolution Paths
children.description: Low-effort primary routes engineered for autonomous or proactive completion

children.name: Primary Self-Service Golden Path
children.description: Zero-escalation digital or conversational AI path resolving the customer need on first contact

children.name: Proactive Pre-Contact Deflection Path
children.description: Center-initiated notification path that resolves a known disruption before the customer initiates contact

children.name: Context-Hydrated Assisted Golden Path
children.description: Planned digital pre-collection followed by warm transfer to a specialist agent for high-complexity intents

children.name: Recovery, Compliance & Degradation Paths
children.description: Pre-planned contingency branches when primary paths encounter friction, risk, or system constraints

children.name: Assisted Service Recovery Path
children.description: High-empathy escalation route triggered after prior service failure or SLA breach

children.name: Regulatory & Compliance Mandatory Path
children.description: Non-bypassable identity verification, consent capture, and verbatim disclosure sequence

children.name: Designed Graceful Degradation Branch
children.description: Planned fallback to scheduled callback or asynchronous messaging during queue surges or backend downtime

facets.name: Normative Targets & Guardrail Budgets
facets.description: Quantitative performance thresholds and friction ceilings embedded directly into blueprint stages

children.name: Latency & Customer Effort Ceilings
children.description: Hard upper bounds on customer time and cognitive effort across journey stages

children.name: Stage Transition Latency SLA Ceiling
children.description: Maximum allowed elapsed time between stage entry and completion across synchronous or asynchronous waits

children.name: Maximum Channel-Hop Budget
children.description: Normative cap on modality switches allowed within a single journey (typically at most 1 planned switch)

children.name: Zero-Repetition Effort Guardrail
children.description: Blueprint invariant forbidding re-collection of identity or slot data already captured in an earlier stage

children.name: Containment & Sentiment Milestones
children.description: Target quality and resolution checkpoints across the blueprint

children.name: Stage Containment Rate Gate
children.description: Planned percentage of arrivals expected to complete self-service at a given stage without escalation

children.name: Expected Sentiment Inflection Milestone
children.description: Blueprint stage where customer sentiment is designed to shift from anxious or frustrated to reassured

facets.name: Blueprint Lifecycle & Simulation Governance
facets.description: Design methodology, simulation stress-testing, versioning, and closed-loop recalibration from empirical telemetry

children.name: Hypothesis Design & Digital Twin Simulation
children.description: Pre-deployment validation of journey blueprints against historical arrival and capacity models

children.name: Hypothesis-Driven Stage Design
children.description: Framing every blueprint change with falsifiable predictions on containment, FCR, and CSAT

children.name: Digital Twin Capacity Stress-Testing
children.description: Simulating blueprint routing and escalation branches against WFM staffing and queue arrival spikes

children.name: Variant Versioning & Closed-Loop Recalibration
children.description: Controlled rollout and continuous refinement of blueprints using Plane 2 process-mining telemetry

children.name: A-B Blueprint Variant Versioning
children.description: Running controlled cohort experiments comparing two prescriptive journey blueprints in production

children.name: Closed-Loop Telemetry Recalibration
children.description: Systematic revision of Plane 1 stage budgets and fallback paths when Plane 2 exposes persistent conformance drift

metrics.name: Target Blueprint First-Contact Resolution Rate
metrics.definition: Normative target percentage of customer journeys designed to achieve full resolution on the primary Golden Path without follow-up contacts

metrics.name: Planned Self-Service Containment Budget
metrics.definition: Prescriptive share of journey arrivals budgeted to resolve autonomously inside digital, IVR, or CAI swimlanes

metrics.name: Normative End-to-End Journey SLA Target
metrics.definition: Planned proportion of customer journeys completing all stages within their cumulative stage latency SLA budget

metrics.name: Budgeted Assisted Transition Wait Ceiling
metrics.definition: Maximum planned customer wait time when transitioning from self-service swimlanes into an assisted agent queue

metrics.name: Budgeted Assisted Stage Handle Time
metrics.definition: Planned agent handle time budget for escalated stages assuming full omnichannel context hydration from prior stages

metrics.name: Target Moment-of-Truth CSAT Benchmark
metrics.definition: Prescriptive customer satisfaction benchmark assigned to critical Moment of Truth nodes in the journey blueprint

scoringModel.name: Prescriptive Journey Blueprint Completeness Scorecard
scoringModel.note: Evaluates whether a Plane 1 Customer Journey Blueprint is production-ready, machine-auditable by Plane 2 (journey_tracking), and actionable by Plane 3 (journey_orchestration).

dimensions.name: Persona & JTBD Outcome Clarity
dimensions.description: Outside-in framing of customer personas, entry preconditions, and customer-verified exit resolution criteria
sampleCriteria: Defines customer Job-to-be-Done independent of internal org chart
Specifies verifiable exit resolution criterion beyond single-channel wrap-up
Identifies critical Moments of Truth and target emotion trajectory

dimensions.name: Exception & Fallback Branch Completeness
dimensions.description: Explicit engineering of non-happy paths including low AI confidence, authentication failures, queue surges, and policy denials
sampleCriteria: Every self-service stage defines a deterministic warm-escalation fallback branch
Includes graceful degradation routes for out-of-hours or WFM staffing deficits
Covers regulatory and fraud step-up verification branches

dimensions.name: Omnichannel & Backstage Handoff Contracts
dimensions.description: Specification of context envelope propagation across channel swimlanes and backstage CRM, KM, and A2A dependencies
sampleCriteria: Mandates canonical context envelope fields at every channel or agent boundary
Maps backstage API and A2A specialist latency dependencies to frontstage stages
Enforces zero-repetition invariant on customer-supplied slots

dimensions.name: Quantitative Stage Budgets & Guardrails
dimensions.description: Assignment of measurable latency SLA ceilings, maximum channel-hop caps, and containment targets to each stage
sampleCriteria: Assigns explicit latency and wait budgets to every stage transition
Caps planned channel switches and authentication prompts
Links stage targets directly to engine KPI identifiers

dimensions.name: Telemetry Observability & Recalibration Hooks
dimensions.description: Instrumentation bindings enabling Plane 2 conformance checking and Plane 3 real-time drift intervention
sampleCriteria: Every blueprint stage emits a deterministic stage_id and blueprint_version tag
Defines drift thresholds that trigger Plane 3 real-time orchestration saves
Schedules periodic recalibration reviews against Plane 2 process-mining findings

failureModes.name: Happy-Path Delusion (Ignoring Exception Branches)
failureModes.signal: Blueprint documents only the ideal self-service Golden Path; 35%+ of live traffic hits unmapped exceptions and drops into generic default queues
failureModes.mitigation: Mandate explicit fallback and exception branches for every stage node as a hard gate in the blueprint completeness rubric

failureModes.name: Inside-Out Org-Chart Mapping
failureModes.signal: Journey stages mirror internal department silos (Billing, Tech Support, Retention) rather than customer Jobs-to-be-Done, institutionalizing transfers
failureModes.mitigation: Anchor all blueprint stages on customer JTBD milestones and require cross-functional backstage choreography beneath unified frontstage steps

failureModes.name: Static Slideware Decay
failureModes.signal: Journey maps live as static design PDFs disconnected from production routing rules and telemetry; actual flows diverge within weeks of launch
failureModes.mitigation: Publish blueprints as versioned machine-readable graphs bound directly to Plane 2 conformance monitors and Plane 3 state machines

failureModes.name: Unbudgeted Backstage System Latency
failureModes.signal: Frontstage blueprint promises instant resolution while backstage fulfillment requires manual back-office queues or slow legacy batch jobs
failureModes.mitigation: Map backstage system and A2A execution SLAs into cumulative stage latency budgets and stress-test against WFM capacity models

failureModes.name: Missing Cross-Channel Handoff Contracts
failureModes.signal: Blueprint arrows connect Web App to Voice Queue without specifying identity binding or context payload, causing 100% context reset on escalation
failureModes.mitigation: Require canonical omnichannel context envelope specifications on every cross-swimlane transition edge

failureModes.name: Vanity Single-Channel Resolution Definitions
failureModes.signal: Blueprint marks journey complete when a bot displays a FAQ link or an agent closes a ticket, even though the underlying customer problem persists
failureModes.mitigation: Define normative exit resolution criteria using customer-verified JTBD completion and zero repeat contact within a 7-day window

exchanges: Versioned prescriptive stage graphs, Golden Path specifications, and stage SLA budgets published as the normative baseline for conformance checking
Empirical drift vectors, shadow escalation paths, and bottleneck telemetry ingested to recalibrate blueprint versions
Machine-readable stage transition rules, Moment-of-Truth flags, and designed fallback branches compiled into real-time execution policies
A-B blueprint variant performance and live intervention outcomes returned to refine prescriptive path designs
Prescriptive context-bridge contracts defining required identity, intent, and slot fields at each planned channel switch
Channel continuity validation telemetry confirming whether planned swimlane handoffs preserve state
Expected emotion trajectories and Moment-of-Truth survey placement specifications shared for listening-post design
Customer effort scores, verbatim pain points, and JTBD gap analyses fed into blueprint redesign cycles
Self-service and agent-assisted blueprint stages linked to required canonical knowledge articles and RAG collections
Content gap signals from failed self-service stages prioritized in the knowledge authoring backlog
Planned stage arrival volumes, assisted escalation percentages, and target SLA ceilings shared for capacity forecasting
Staffing constraints and intraday shrinkage boundaries incorporated into graceful degradation branch designs
